title: Client Connector logs: verbosity, user access and collection

prose.text: Client Connector writes its own logs on the device, and three separate settings decide how much it writes, what the user may do with them, and how they reach support.

steps.label: What is in them.
steps.text: [[zcc.logs.client-log]] and, for traffic flows on Windows, [[zcc.logs.flow-logging]].

checks.do: For a question about what a user did on the web or which rule acted, go to the ZIA or ZPA logs, not the client log.

cloud-logs-independent.statement: The client's logging settings govern how the app generates logs and what users may do with them; no source ties ZIA or ZPA cloud logging to them, so hiding or reducing client logs does not imply less cloud logging.
cloud-logs-independent.conditions: Rests on absence: the logging-control and app-profile articles describe only the app's own logs, and no captured source links them to ZIA or ZPA log generation.

quotes: Using App Profiles, you can determine how the app generates logs.
